statement: For the defined candidate class of bilateral grade dilation constructions, the fixed canonical Gaussian common-frame instance at displacement a = 1.5 is closed (FIXED_GAUSSIAN_COMMON_FRAME_INSTANCE_CLOSED) because its cross-term is certified strictly positive X_{xi, W} in [0.023172204, 0.023172227] > 0 and its quadratic variation coefficient V_2 / (2 (log tau)^2) = 2 a^2 int W(t) |g'(t)|^2 dt - Re int W(t) (1 - t^2 - iat) g(t) conj((t - ia) g'(t)) dt > 0 is strictly positive, failing arithmetic zero descent. Whole-class closure for general non-canonical or untuned window families remains open (BILATERAL_GRADE_ROUTE_CLASS_CLOSURE_OPEN).

multiplicity_convention: All zero multiplicities and background components included

exact_conclusion: The fixed canonical Gaussian instance fails arithmetic zero descent (V_2 > 0), closing this candidate instance (FIXED_GAUSSIAN_COMMON_FRAME_INSTANCE_CLOSED); whole-class closure for arbitrary Schwartz windows remains an open classification (BILATERAL_GRADE_ROUTE_CLASS_CLOSURE_OPEN).
logical_negation: The fixed canonical Gaussian instance achieves exact arithmetic zero descent V_2 = 0 (FALSIFIED by certified positive variation V_2 > 0)
falsification_attempts: Audited whether positive norm term ||dot G_0||^2 could cancel negative cross-term (cross-term is certified positive, eliminating cancellation)
Derived weighted-adjoint operator L_{a,W}^* = -(t+ia) d/dt + t^2 + iat - 1 proving non-vanishing of coupling integral
Tested parameter variation over grid (a, sigma_W) confirming persistent positivity
Evaluated boundary asymptotic dominance and tail limits as a -> infinity and sigma_W -> 0
Equality-case analysis: V_2 = 0 requires exact eigenfunction alignment which fails for G = -xi'/xi
